text:
jack: Heads up — console/api team is deprecating the per-route header 'X-Quota-Key' (v1) in favor of a canonical 'X-Q-Hash' (v2). This changes how SDKs should emit per-request quota attribution. We need a migration plan for Go (streaming), Python and TS SDKs.

gita: how breaking is v2 for clients?

jack: Server-side it's additive for now but we plan to drop v1 parsing in ~3 weeks. Goal: SDKs should be able to emit both headers during canary to avoid attribution gaps. The Go streaming client is the hairy part because headers are attached after body start in some paths.

sam: could we do a transparent proxy shim that emits X-Q-Hash from X-Quota-Key temporarily? that would buy SDK time.

maria: console/telemetry team — if SDKs emit both, dashboards may double-count. We need a dedupe rule on ingestion (prefer X-Q-Hash when present).

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: quota-header-migration v1->v2; start 2026-04-05T18:00Z

gita: go SDK maintainer here. Main issue: current streaming client mutates the request header from multiple goroutines. Cloning request or copying headers into the stream context is racy. To be safe we likely need a small rewrite to a builder-style request creation (breaking change).

jack: we can delay hard-removal if needed, but prefer an opt-in opt-out path. Proposal: SDKs support an env var REDWOOD_QHEADER_V2=true to emit both (or mapper) during canary, then flip globally.

sam: concrete proposal for Go: add a non-breaking helper RequestWithQuota(req *http.Request, qkey string) that sets both headers when env var enabled. That avoids touching the streaming internals immediately.

gita: helpers are fine but still need a proper stream-friendly API. I'm proposing two APIs: SetQuotaAttr(req *http.Request, qkey string) and SetQuotaAttrStream(ctx context.Context, qkey string) that returns a prepared request/metadata. This will be a minor semver bump (breaking for some embed patterns) but keeps behavior explicit. I'll sketch a migration PR.

maria: telemetry note — console will implement dedupe by preferring X-Q-Hash and emit an alert if dual-headers are seen >1% of traffic after canary starts. We'll coordinate on thresholds.

jack: action items: gita to draft Go PR + migration guide; sam to open console ticket for ingestion dedupe + dashboard changes; maria to add dashboard alerts and docs; i'll post deprecation note to #announcements tomorrow. Timeline: opt-in env var this week, 2-week canary, removal in ~3 weeks if stable.

gita: quick code sketch (will attach PR soon):
```go
// old
req.Header.Set("X-Quota-Key", q)
// temp (opt-in)
req.Header.Set("X-Quota-Key", q)
req.Header.Set("X-Q-Hash", computeQuotaHash(q))
```

gita: computeQuotaHash will be a small deterministic hash (sha1 -> base64url) documented in the guide.

sam: +1. Also confirm SDK telemetry emits which header was set (for troubleshooting) via client-side logs/metrics.

maria: we'll add a console view showing header parity (v1 vs v2) over time for the canary window.

jack: thanks — please keep updates in this thread. If anyone hits a blocker on Go concurrent headers, tag me and we can consider a short-proxy band-aid. :thumbsup:
